newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi signs $177.6 mln in deals with medical firms.
newsitem.headline: Saudi signs $177.6 mln in deals with medical firms.

text.p: Saudi Arabia, enjoying rising revenue from higher oil prices, on Monday signed 156 deals with pharmaceutical companies worth 666 million riyals ($177.6 million) which would be paid in 1996.
Saudi television news said the pharmaceutical suppliers were asked to meet delievery dates and present bills on time "for payment in the current fiscal year (calander 1996)."
It was not immediately clear if the payments would cover part of outstanding debts to pharmaceutical firms.
In recent years Riyadh, the world's largest oil producer and exporter, has suffered cash shortages which resulted in large debts to various suppliers, farmers and others.

But Saudi Arabian planners said the kingdom has given a priority in 1996 to using added revenue from higher than forecast world oil prices to pay part of the outstanding debt and meet new obligations on time.

Earlier on Monday industry sources and bankers said the kingdom, one of the Middle East's top pharmaceutical consumers, had started paying part of hundreds of millions of dollars in arrears to international suppliers.
They said the payments to suppliers mostly from Europe and the United States had started in the last week of August.
Saudi Arabia also started paying more than three billion riyals to holders of special farmers' certificates on maturity on August 31, in a further sign of Riyadh's improving finances.
